findings.topic: Vault path resolution gotcha (operational, relevant to bead authors)
findings.detail: authfile.DefaultVaultPath() (internal/authfile/authfile.go:336-347) resolves via CAAM_HOME > XDG_DATA_HOME > os.UserHomeDir()+'.local/share/caam/vault'. In this sandbox, the ambient $HOME was /home/ubuntu/orch-homes/cc-cabot (a per-profile shallow-spawn sub-home with its OWN empty vault), NOT the real /home/ubuntu account home where the actual multi-profile vault lives. Any cold agent re-running `caam monitor` must run with HOME=/home/ubuntu (or whatever the real operator home is) or it will see zero profiles.
findings.evidence: `./caam monitor --format json --once` under the ambient shallow-spawn HOME printed `{"profiles": null}`. Real vault confirmed at /home/ubuntu/.local/share/caam/vault with claude/{arthur,benson,cabot,saumil,saumil_2}@feta.fund and codex/{arthur,saumil}@feta.fund subdirs.

findings.topic: All 5 Claude vault credential copies are expired-on-disk access tokens (root cause of 401s)
findings.detail: Every vault claude profile's .credentials.json has an accessToken (108 chars, prefix sk-ant-o) whose expiresAt (epoch-ms) is already in the past relative to probe time (2026-07-03 ~19:58 UTC): arthur -15073s, benson -14712s, cabot -34348s, saumil_2 -34102s, saumil -14903s (all STALE by 4.1h-9.5h). All have refreshToken present and identical scopes ['user:file_upload','user:inference','user:mcp_servers','user:profile','user:sessions:claude_code']. monitor.go's readAccessToken (internal/monitor/monitor.go:288-315) reads this raw accessToken from the vault copy and never checks expiresAt or attempts a refresh before calling ClaudeFetcher.Fetch (internal/usage/claude.go:44).
findings.evidence: Python JSON parse of each vault .credentials.json's claudeAiOauth.expiresAt vs `date +%s`=1783108696 (2026-07-03T19:58:16Z).

findings.topic: The real live ~/.claude credential file is ALSO stale on disk — but the actual `claude` CLI silently refreshes at launch and does NOT write that refresh back to the vault
findings.detail: The live system-wide /home/ubuntu/.claude/.credentials.json currently holds benson's expiresAt exactly (1783093983209, STALE by ~14743s) confirming it's the last-active profile's stale snapshot. But the per-profile shallow-spawn home for cc-cabot (/home/ubuntu/orch-homes/cc-cabot/.claude/.credentials.json), which the user's `caam shallow-spawn cc-cabot -- claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` populated and the live `claude` binary then used, has expiresAt=1783136626135 -> delta +27877s (FRESH, valid ~7.7h from now) — i.e. a DIFFERENT, newer access token than the vault's cabot@feta.fund copy (expiresAt=1783074347278, STALE by -34401s / ~9.5h ago). This is direct proof that Claude Code refreshes its OAuth token transparently on/after spawn using the refreshToken, but caam's vault snapshot of that profile is never updated with the refreshed token — vault copies are frozen at whatever moment they were last written (e.g. at profile-switch/backup time) and go stale on their own natural ~5h+ cadence.
findings.evidence: Compared expiresAt fields of /home/ubuntu/orch-homes/cc-cabot/.claude/.credentials.json (FRESH, delta +27877s) vs /home/ubuntu/.local/share/caam/vault/claude/cabot@feta.fund/.credentials.json (STALE, delta -34401s) at the same instant.

findings.topic: Live probe: stale vault Claude tokens return clean 401, never a durable per-account 429
findings.detail: GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage with headers exactly matching internal/usage/claude.go:60-63 (Authorization: Bearer <tok>, anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20, User-Agent: caam/1.0, Accept: application/json), issued individually (>=2s apart) against arthur's and saumil's stale vault tokens (the two accounts the user's original monitor run reported as '429'): both returned HTTP 401 with body `{"type":"error","error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"Invalid authentication credentials", ...}}` — the SAME response class as benson/cabot/saumil_2. No Retry-After header, no rate-limit headers present on either 401.
findings.evidence: curl -D header dumps: both requests -> `HTTP/2 401`, content-type application/json, body error.type=authentication_error. Zero 429s reproduced in isolated single-token, spaced probing.

findings.topic: 429 root cause: unthrottled concurrent burst, not a per-account condition
findings.detail: internal/monitor/monitor.go's Refresh() (around line 200) launches one goroutine per PROVIDER, and internal/usage/multi.go's FetchAllProfiles (multi.go:55, goroutine at multi.go:66) launches one goroutine PER PROFILE inside that, with zero stagger, backoff, or concurrency limit. This means all 5 Claude profiles' GETs to api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage fire within microseconds of each other, from the same process/IP, with the identical static User-Agent 'caam/1.0'. Since isolated re-probing of arthur/saumil (the '429' accounts from the user's run) now cleanly returns 401 with no rate-limit signal, the 429s the user saw are best explained as Anthropic's API rate-limiter reacting to the simultaneous 5-request burst — which 2 of the 5 land on is a nondeterministic scheduling/ordering artifact of the burst, not a property of those 2 accounts' tokens.
findings.evidence: Code: internal/monitor/monitor.go Refresh() wg/goroutine loop (~line 200); internal/usage/multi.go:55-108 per-profile goroutine loop with no rate limiting. Live evidence: arthur and saumil both return 401 (not 429) when probed alone with >=2s spacing.

findings.topic: Live fresh-token probe: real Anthropic usage API response shape (from valid cc-cabot token)
findings.detail: GET .../api/oauth/usage with the FRESH cc-cabot token returned HTTP 200. Top-level JSON keys: five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_oauth_apps, seven_day_opus, seven_day_sonnet, seven_day_cowork, seven_day_omelette, tangelo, iguana_necktie, omelette_promotional, nimbus_quill, cinder_cove, amber_ladder, extra_usage, limits, spend, member_dashboard_available. five_hour and seven_day each have {utilization, resets_at, limit_dollars, used_dollars, remaining_dollars}. All the 'seven_day_*' and codenamed keys (tangelo, iguana_necktie, nimbus_quill, cinder_cove, amber_ladder, seven_day_cowork, seven_day_omelette, seven_day_oauth_apps) were null for this account — no key literally named 'fable' or 'Fable' anywhere in the response. No 'five_hour_opus' or 'five_hour_<model>' analogs were observed — only weekly (seven_day_X) per-model-ish buckets exist in the schema, when populated.
findings.evidence: curl to https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage with fresh cc-cabot orch-home token -> HTTP/2 200; `python3 -c "json.load(...).keys()"` produced the key list above; per-key one-level nesting dumped (five_hour/seven_day shown, all others NoneType for this account).

findings.topic: Existing Claude parser bug: 'opus' JSON tag doesn't match the real API field
findings.detail: internal/usage/claude.go:36 declares `Opus *claudeWindow \`json:"opus"\`` and claude.go:127-137 maps it to info.TertiaryWindow, but the live API's actual field name is `seven_day_opus` (confirmed in the probe above), not `opus`. This means TertiaryWindow (the only existing scaffold for a premium/per-model Claude window) currently NEVER populates from the real API — it's dead code today, independent of the auth-staleness bug. This is directly relevant to deliverable 2 (surfacing Fable/Opus-style per-model Claude usage): the existing plumbing is wired to the wrong key and also has no field at all for a matching 'five_hour_opus'-equivalent bucket.
findings.evidence: Code: internal/usage/claude.go:36 (json:"opus"), :127-137 (TertiaryWindow assignment). Live evidence: real response's top-level keys include 'seven_day_opus' but no 'opus' key at all.

findings.topic: Codex tokens are long-lived JWTs and were NOT the source of any auth error in the original report
findings.detail: Both codex vault auth.json access_tokens (arthur, saumil) are JWTs whose 'exp' claim is far in the future: arthur delta +270485s (~3.1 days FRESH), saumil delta +481050s (~5.6 days FRESH). Both were last refreshed by their real OpenAI CLI on 2026-06-26 and 2026-06-29 respectively (last_refresh field) yet remain valid — OpenAI's Codex/ChatGPT tokens simply have a much longer lifetime than Claude's ~5h OAuth access tokens, so vault staleness is a non-issue for Codex today.
findings.evidence: Base64-decoded JWT payload (locally, token never printed) exp claims vs current epoch 1783108696+; auth.json last_refresh timestamps 2026-06-26T23:10:19Z and 2026-06-29T09:39:44Z.

findings.topic: Codex 'unknown' WARN status root cause: nil AuthPool wired into monitor command (separate bug from auth)
findings.detail: cmd/caam/cmd/monitor.go:116 declares `var pool *authpool.AuthPool` and NEVER assigns/constructs it anywhere in that command (no authpool.NewAuthPool(...), no LoadFromVault) before passing it at monitor.go:135 `monitor.WithAuthPool(pool)` — i.e. a permanently-nil pool is injected. In internal/monitor/monitor.go buildProfileState (line 318), `if m.pool != nil { state.PoolStatus = m.pool.GetStatus(provider, name) }` is skipped entirely since m.pool is nil, so PoolStatus stays at its zero-value default authpool.PoolStatusUnknown (set at monitor.go:324) for EVERY profile of EVERY provider, always. The table renderer (internal/monitor/render_table.go:71 `status := p.PoolStatus.String()`) prints this literally as 'unknown' — but ONLY on the success-render branch, i.e. only when usageUnavailable() (alerts.go:73-84) returns empty because the usage fetch actually succeeded. For Claude today, usage fetches are failing (401), so the table takes the OTHER branch (alerts.go:91 shortUsageError -> 'auth expired (re-login)') which never touches PoolStatus, masking this bug for Claude. For Codex, fetches succeed (confirmed live: 200 OK with real usage data), so the bug is directly visible as '...% | unknown'. IMPORTANT for deliverable-1 sequencing: once the Claude auth/staleness bug is fixed and Claude fetches start succeeding, this SAME nil-pool bug will make Claude rows also start showing '| unknown' unless fixed in the same pass — this is a shared/compounding bug, not codex-specific, it's just presently invisible for Claude.
findings.evidence: cmd/caam/cmd/monitor.go:116 (`var pool *authpool.AuthPool`, never assigned) and :135 (`monitor.WithAuthPool(pool)`); internal/monitor/monitor.go:318-334 (buildProfileState nil-check + default PoolStatusUnknown at :324); internal/monitor/render_table.go:71; internal/authpool/pool.go:136-145 (GetStatus doc: 'Returns PoolStatusUnknown if the profile is not in the pool'). Cross-check: /home/ubuntu/.local/share/caam/auth_pool_state.json has `"profiles": {}` (empty) confirming nothing populates the pool today, and no `caam` daemon process is running (`ps aux` showed no daemon/poolMonitor process) so nothing else is filling it in the background either. Contrast with cmd/caam/cmd/pool.go:73 which DOES properly do `authpool.NewAuthPool(authpool.WithVault(vault))` — showing the correct pattern that monitor.go should mirror.

findings.topic: Codex per-model usage (GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark) IS exposed by the live API, in an array the current parser ignores
findings.detail: Live GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage (headers mirrored from internal/usage/codex.go:123-128: Authorization Bearer, User-Agent caam/1.0, Accept application/json, plus ChatGPT-Account-Id) with a codex vault token returned HTTP 200 and a top-level `additional_rate_limits` array containing exactly one entry: `{"limit_name": "GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark", "metered_feature": "codex_bengalfox", "rate_limit": {"allowed":..., "primary_window": {used_percent, limit_window_seconds:18000 (5h), reset_after_seconds, reset_at}, "secondary_window": {used_percent, limit_window_seconds:604800 (7d/weekly), reset_after_seconds, reset_at}}}`. This is a literal, unambiguous match for the user's requested 'GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark usage (5H and weekly)' deliverable. However internal/usage/codex.go's `codexUsageResponse` struct (codex.go:35-38: fields PlanType, RateLimit, Credits only) has NO field mapping to `additional_rate_limits` at all — this per-model bucket is currently silently discarded by json.Decode (extra unmapped keys are ignored by default encoding/json behavior), never reaching UsageInfo or the table.
findings.evidence: curl to https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage with arthur's codex vault token (mirroring codex.go headers) -> HTTP/2 200; response body's `additional_rate_limits[0]` verbatim keys: limit_name='GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark', metered_feature='codex_bengalfox', nested rate_limit.primary_window.limit_window_seconds=18000, secondary_window.limit_window_seconds=604800. Code: internal/usage/codex.go:35-38 (codexUsageResponse struct has no additional_rate_limits field).

findings.topic: Codex top-level rate_limit (the one currently parsed) confirms primary=5h / secondary=weekly convention
findings.detail: The account-wide (non-per-model) `rate_limit.primary_window.limit_window_seconds` = 18000 (exactly 5 hours) and `secondary_window.limit_window_seconds` = 604800 (exactly 7 days), which is the same convention already assumed by internal/usage/codex.go:161-179 (WindowDuration set directly from the API's limit_window_seconds, not hardcoded) — so the EXISTING top-level parsing logic is correct and can be reused as-is for the new additional_rate_limits[...].rate_limit sub-object; no new duration-inference logic is needed, just a new struct field + a name/feature match for 'GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark' (or a case-insensitive 'spark'/'codex-spark' match, and ideally also match by `metered_feature` in case the human-readable limit_name changes) plus population of two new UsageWindow slots (or reuse of a per-model map, see usage.go:53's existing but unused-for-Claude 'PerModel' style comment) for presentation.
findings.evidence: Live JSON: primary_window.limit_window_seconds=18000, secondary_window.limit_window_seconds=604800 both at top-level rate_limit and inside additional_rate_limits[0].rate_limit. Code: internal/usage/codex.go:161-179 WindowDuration assignment; internal/usage/usage.go:53 comment referencing per-model map concept.

hypotheses.hypothesis: PRIME HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED: All 5 Claude vault credential copies hold expired-on-disk access tokens because caam's vault snapshot is written once (at backup/switch time) and never updated when the live Claude Code CLI silently refreshes its OAuth token via the refreshToken on subsequent launches; monitor's readAccessToken() reads that frozen, stale snapshot directly with no expiry check and no refresh-before-use logic.
hypotheses.evidence: All 5 vault .credentials.json files have expiresAt in the past (4.1h-9.5h stale) at probe time; the live orch-home for cc-cabot (post real `claude` launch) has a FRESH, differently-valued token than the vault's cabot@feta.fund copy at the identical instant; isolated GETs with the stale vault tokens deterministically return 401 authentication_error; the same token used fresh (orch-home) deterministically returns 200 with full usage data.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The 429s reported for arthur/saumil in the user's original monitor run were NOT a distinct per-account condition (e.g. not 'valid token but rate-limited', not 'differently-stale token') but an artifact of monitor.go/multi.go firing all 5 Claude profile GETs concurrently with zero stagger/backoff against the same Anthropic endpoint from the same process — a burst that can trip Anthropic's own rate limiter nondeterministically for whichever requests land in a given microsecond window.
hypotheses.evidence: Re-probing arthur and saumil individually with >=2s spacing both returned clean 401 (not 429), matching the other 3 accounts' behavior exactly; code confirms an unthrottled per-profile goroutine fan-out in multi.go:55-108 with no concurrency limiting, no jitter, no shared rate limiter across the burst. Not logically provable as the sole cause without re-triggering the exact original 5-way concurrent burst (which the security/request-budget rules for this task disallow), but it is the most parsimonious explanation consistent with all gathered evidence and standard API rate-limiter behavior.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The Codex 'unknown' WARN status is a completely independent bug from the Claude auth issue: it's caused by cmd/caam/cmd/monitor.go injecting a nil *authpool.AuthPool into the Monitor, which makes PoolStatus permanently default to Unknown for every profile of every provider; it is only visible for Codex today because Codex's usage fetches succeed (reaching the render branch that prints PoolStatus), while Claude's fetches currently fail and take a different render branch that never touches PoolStatus.
hypotheses.evidence: cmd/caam/cmd/monitor.go:116 declares `var pool *authpool.AuthPool` with no subsequent assignment anywhere in the file, passed as-is to WithAuthPool at :135; monitor.go's buildProfileState nil-guards on m.pool (never populating PoolStatus) and defaults to PoolStatusUnknown; render_table.go only prints PoolStatus.String() in the branch taken when usageUnavailable() returns empty (i.e. usage fetch succeeded); live auth_pool_state.json has zero entries and no caam daemon process is running to populate it via any other path.

hypotheses.hypothesis: GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark per-model usage (5H + weekly) is available today from the wham/usage endpoint via the additional_rate_limits array, and can be added to the Codex fetcher/table with a small, additive parser change (no redesign) since the nested rate_limit sub-object reuses the exact same primary_window/secondary_window shape already parsed for the top-level window.
hypotheses.evidence: Live probe of chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage returned additional_rate_limits[0] with limit_name='GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark', metered_feature='codex_bengalfox', and rate_limit.primary_window/secondary_window in the identical shape (used_percent, limit_window_seconds, reset_after_seconds, reset_at) as the already-parsed top-level rate_limit.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A Claude 'Fable' per-model usage bucket may not be safely identifiable today: the live oauth/usage response contains several opaque, currently-null, internally-codenamed keys (tangelo, iguana_necktie, omelette_promotional, nimbus_quill, cinder_cove, amber_ladder, seven_day_cowork, seven_day_omelette, seven_day_oauth_apps) plus a clearly-named but currently-unwired seven_day_opus, but none is literally labeled 'fable', and all were null for the one live account tested (no recent Opus/premium-model usage on that account to populate a candidate key).
hypotheses.evidence: Full top-level key enumeration of the live 200 OK response from a fresh cc-cabot token; every non-five_hour/seven_day key was JSON null for this account, giving no way to disambiguate which (if any) codename corresponds to Fable without either official API documentation or a probe against an account that has actually consumed Fable/Opus-tier usage recently.

open_questions: Which of the opaque codenamed keys in the Claude oauth/usage response (tangelo, iguana_necktie, omelette_promotional, nimbus_quill, cinder_cove, amber_ladder, seven_day_cowork, seven_day_omelette, seven_day_oauth_apps) — if any — corresponds to 'Fable' specifically; this could only be resolved by probing an account/token that has actually used the Fable model recently (so the corresponding key becomes non-null) or by finding official API documentation/changelog naming the mapping. Recommend beads spec a defensive/graceful-omit implementation per D4 rather than guessing the mapping.

Whether Anthropic's API applies the observed 429 rate limiting per-IP, per-token, or per-User-Agent, and what the exact threshold/window is — not conclusively determined here since reproducing the original 5-way concurrent burst was avoided to respect the 'max ~6 requests, spaced >=2s' security constraint. If a bead implementer wants harder proof, a controlled test firing exactly 5 concurrent GETs (all from stale-but-distinct tokens) against the real endpoint, one time, would be the direct confirmation step — but note this itself would consume real API rate-limit budget and should probably just be accepted as inferred rather than re-tested.

Whether refreshing and persisting vault Claude tokens back after a live refresh (the leaning-recommendation D2 fix direction) is safe/desired given caam's design intent for the vault to be a static backup/rotation store vs. a live-synced credential cache — this is a design decision for the fix-spec bead to make explicit with rationale, not something resolvable from runtime evidence alone.

Whether the shared nil-AuthPool bug (cmd/caam/cmd/monitor.go:116) should be fixed by properly constructing+loading a real AuthPool (mirroring cmd/caam/cmd/pool.go:73's authpool.NewAuthPool(authpool.WithVault(vault)) pattern, then LoadFromVault), noting LoadFromVault itself only sets status to 'Unknown' too per its own doc comment (authpool/pool.go:510-511) so further validation/health wiring may still be needed — or whether the simpler/more minimal-lift fix is to have render_table.go stop rendering a bare pool-status column when PoolStatus is Unknown (e.g., omit it or derive a friendlier fallback from health/usage data instead), which better matches the 'minimal lift, no redesign' constraint (D2/deliverable-2 constraints).
